name: source-qualified Gmail draft-send ambiguity reconciliation classification

official_sources.finding: A Draft is a container with a stable draft ID while its underlying message ID changes on replacement. When a draft is sent, Gmail deletes the draft and creates a new message with an updated ID and SENT label; drafts.send returns that new Message.
drafts.send sends an existing draft and returns a Message on success.
Drafts/messages can be placed in a thread using the drafts/messages resources; membership requires target threadId, RFC-compliant References/In-Reply-To, and matching Subject.

create_draft.reply_support: reply_message_id can create a threaded reply

successful_send_with_response.reason: send_draft returns the new sent-message identity when response is received

recipe: Before send, retain stable draft_id, the target existing thread identity, and an application op_id in subject/body.
After ambiguous completion, read the target thread and look for exactly one SENT message containing the exact op_id; if found, classify DONE and do not resend.

Also inspect draft presence as secondary evidence: official semantics say successful send deletes the draft, but absence alone is not accepted as proof because connector/API visibility timing was not established here.

If sent op_id is absent and draft appears present, do not claim safe retry from source evidence alone; without a linearizability/visibility guarantee the conservative state is UNKNOWN until stronger evidence is available.
ambiguous_send_of_existing_thread_reply.why_better_than_global_search: A reply has a pre-existing target thread, so read_email_thread scopes reconciliation to a stable conversation identity instead of depending only on mailbox-wide search indexing.

ambiguous_send_of_standalone_new_message.reason: The response would reveal the new Message/thread identity, but if that response is lost this connector exposes no history-list action and no caller idempotency key. Searching a unique op_id can discover success but no source inspected here gives an exact consistency bound that makes absence safe proof of non-send.

critical_boundary: A stable draft ID is not a post-send idempotency key: successful send destroys the draft resource and creates a new Message ID. Therefore blindly retrying send_draft after an ambiguous outcome is not justified by draft identity alone.

phase1_assessment.acceptance: No new exactly-once external-send route is accepted. Thread-scoped evidence can reduce ambiguity for replies, but opaque caller-keyless sends remain an unresolved child.

next_test: No live Gmail send is authorized in this CLEAN role. If a future authorized isolated mailbox fixture is available, precommit a threaded-reply op_id, inject response loss, then measure whether thread read and draft visibility are immediately reconciliable. Until then preserve hard-gate semantics.
